title: Worked (JEE Advanced): complex coefficients, no conjugate pair

board_content.text: $2+i$ and $1$ are NOT conjugates — the coefficients are complex.
Check: sum $=3+i$, product $=2+i$. Consistent with Vieta.

segments_english.text: <curious>Now the Advanced case that breaks the comfortable pattern: a quadratic with complex coefficients.</curious>
Solve x squared minus three plus i, times x, plus two plus i, equals zero. Notice the coefficients themselves are complex.
Compute the discriminant. Three plus i, squared, is eight plus six i. Four times two plus i is eight plus four i. Subtracting gives two i.

So we need the square root of two i. Set it equal to x plus i y: x squared minus y squared is zero, two x y is two, and the modulus of two i is two. That gives x squared and y squared both one, with x y positive.
So root of two i is plus or minus one plus i.
Substitute into the formula: x equals three plus i, plus or minus one plus i, all over two. The plus branch gives two plus i; the minus branch gives one.

Here's the punchline: the two roots, two plus i and one, are not conjugates of each other. And that is completely fine, because the coefficients were complex, so the conjugate-root theorem simply does not apply.
Quick check with Vieta: the sum is three plus i and the product is two plus i, both matching the coefficients. Everything is consistent.

segments_hinglish.text: <curious>Ab wo Advanced case jo comfortable pattern todta hai: complex coefficients wali quadratic.</curious>
Solve karo x squared minus three plus i, times x, plus two plus i, equals zero. Dhyaan do coefficients khud complex hain.
Discriminant compute karo. Three plus i, squared, hai eight plus six i. Four times two plus i hai eight plus four i. Subtract karne se milta hai two i.

To humein two i ka square root chahiye. Ise x plus i y ke barabar set karo: x squared minus y squared zero hai, two x y two hai, aur two i ka modulus two hai. Ye deta hai x squared aur y squared dono one, with x y positive.
To root of two i hai plus or minus one plus i.
Formula mein substitute karo: x equals three plus i, plus or minus one plus i, poora over two. Plus branch deta hai two plus i; minus branch deta hai one.
Ye raha punchline: do roots, two plus i aur one, ek doosre ke conjugates nahi hain. Aur ye bilkul theek hai, kyunki coefficients complex the, to conjugate-root theorem bas apply hi nahi hota.
Vieta se quick check: sum hai three plus i aur product hai two plus i, dono coefficients se match. Sab consistent hai.
